title: Cost Autopilot: rulebook, adaptive defaults, and quantization-safety layer
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: teams need safe, conservative automation for cost controls that can be applied across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Previous heuristics were ad-hoc (per-workload scripts) and caused regressions in quality when aggressive quantization + batching were applied without a safety envelope. This PR introduces a first-class 'Cost Autopilot' rulebook and an adaptive defaults engine that: 1) provides conservative batching/caching/quant suggestions scoped per model family and workload shape, 2) applies a quantization-safety layer that prevents high-impact quant transforms for routes flagged as 'safety-critical' by route metadata, and 3) exposes an operator-facing override and rollout path in Redwood Console. Summary of changes: - new rules: redwood/optimizer/autopilot/rulebook.py (core engine + evaluation predicates) - adaptive defaults service: redwood/optimizer/autopilot/engine.py (policy scoring and suggestions API) - quant safety layer: runtime/quant_safety/middleware.py (pre-deploy checks + runtime guardrails) - defaults data: config/autopilot/defaults_v1.yaml (per-model-family default profiles) - console UX: console/src/components/autopilot/RulebookEditor.tsx (UI to review and override rules) - docs: docs/operators/autopilot.md (operator guide + rollout checklist) - tests: tests/autopilot/test_rulebook.py, tests/autopilot/test_quant_safety.py Implementation notes: - Rulebook is a small DSL (YAML-backed) evaluated by predicates (traffic_pct, latency_slo, recent_quality_regressions, model_arch). Rules score suggestion confidence and a simple conflict resolver chooses conservative options when rules disagree. - Adaptive engine samples real request distributions for a rolling 24h window and produces per-route suggested profiles (batch_size, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile). Suggestions are additive (recommend but not applied automatically unless operator enables autopilot mode). - Quant safety layer has two components: (a) preflight: a CI-style check run in model onboarding (rejects quant profiles that fail fidelity thresholds for flagged routes) and (b) runtime guard: a small runtime filter that prevents applying unsafe quantized kernels for hot routes if latency improvements are marginal but expected quality drop is above policy. - Console changes include an 'Autopilot preview' panel with canary rollout controls and a dry-run mode that shows estimated token-cost delta and baseline quality delta derived from offline evals. Checklist: - [x] Rulebook DSL and validator - [x] Adaptive defaults engine + API surface - [x] Quant-safety preflight + runtime guard - [x] Console UI for preview and overrides - [x] Docs and operator rollout guide - [x] Unit tests and integration harness notes Rollout plan: 1) feature flag the autopilot engine off by default; expose to internal dev clusters for 1 week smoke testing. 2) Enable read-only UI for customers with an opt-in toggle. 3) After 2 weeks of monitoring, permit canary auto-apply for non-safety-critical routes at 1% traffic, increasing progressively. Testing: added unit tests and synthetic workloads to CI (tests cover rule resolution, scoring, and a simulated golden dataset for quant safety). Benchmarks: on resnet-chat-13B-like workload we saw 18-24% token-cost saving with conservative defaults (no observed quality regressions on standard eval sets). Backwards compatibility: rulebook defaults are additive and do not change existing route configs until an operator accepts a suggestion or enables autopilot-mode. See docs/operators/autopilot.md for escalation and rollback steps. Related: ENG-1392 (autopilot design), ENG-1410 (quant-safety requirements), SUP-445 (customer ticket that motivated preflight checks).
